# Independent audit of the vertex-normal pencil classification

Source: `candidate 558c9d47421b8323`, Sections 1–5, together with its two exact coefficient JSON artifacts and `supporting computation verify_tetrahedral_vertex_pencil_equal_pair_defect_transport.py`.

**Result: PASS.** The stated positive vertex-normal pencil forces equality of the opposite central pair. Together with the separately audited jointly funded curvature theorem, this excludes the two-full/one-one-zero-row tetrahedral capacity stratum, including the boundary b_1=1/3. It is not a general mixed-integer theorem.

The independent review checked the normalization and all geometric hypotheses. Positive rescaling preserves the sign of the pencil parameter. At a second admitted strict quadrilateral section all denominators in the centroid map are positive; T>0 also makes division by T harmless. I independently verified that the four displayed centroid formulas agree with the reciprocal-diagonal formulas used in the global conic note.

The finite-common-root implication of the two resultants is valid even when a leading coefficient drops after parameter specialization. A common finite root makes the padded Sylvester matrix singular; no assumption that the specialized degree remains four or three is used. The source separately handles the factor B=0 rather than discarding it. The full positive-domain factors in the quartic and cubic resultants were checked against their displayed signs.

For the quartic boundary factor, independent simplification gives

    b_1-1/3 = -q B/[3(q+1)(q+r)(pqr+pq+pr+qr)].

Thus B=0 is exactly the stated boundary. Substitution of p=r(r-q^2)/[q((r+1)q+2r)] independently reproduces both displayed boundary centroid coordinates. The two canceled boundary polynomial contents are respectively q^3 and q^3(q^3+r), strictly positive for the actual domain. The generic canceled contents are the explicitly positive factors displayed in Section 2 of the source.

The sign proof for G is sound. Under p=P sqrt(r), q=Q sqrt(r), R=sqrt(r)+1/sqrt(r), the factor is r^4 times the printed cubic in Q. The actual noncentral inequality gives 0<P<1 and Q<Qmax. Its leading coefficient is positive and each other coefficient is negative. Thus g(Q)/Q^3 is strictly increasing; the exact negative value at Qmax proves G<0 throughout the actual domain. No numerical sign inference is used.

On the B=0 boundary, positivity of p gives q^2<r. Then q^2-q-2r and q^2-qr-2r are strictly negative, and all other displayed nonconstant factors apart from r-1 are nonzero. In H_1, the negative term -2q^2r^2 has magnitude less than 2r^3 and is absorbed by 3r^3. In H_2, -2q^2r is absorbed by 3r^2 in the same way. Hence H_1,H_2 are strictly positive. This verifies the complete boundary sign argument, including possible leading-degree drops.

The exact determinant checker has completed successfully with `--regenerate`: both quartics were rebuilt from the actual geometric centroid formulas and matched coefficient by coefficient; the full three-variable Sylvester factorization, the separately rebuilt boundary cubics and their complete resultant, and the noncentral endpoint identity all passed. I read the fraction-free determinant implementation and the sign/content bookkeeping; it checks an equality of polynomials, not sampled evaluations. The independent local checks above additionally verify the geometric formulas and the canceled boundary contents.

Finally, the incidence application's signs are correct: c^x+c^y=-w m gives -c^y=c^x+w m, precisely the positive pencil with both sections oriented toward the first captured pair. The conclusion b_l=b_m meets every hypothesis of the independently audited joint-Schur funding theorem. No missing global optimality assertion is supplied by stationarity alone.

No repair or unresolved gap was found in the stated theorem.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
